key_insight: TextSeal2 embeds detectable watermarks in LLM-generated text without changing the model’s output distribution. Its watermark survives speculative decoding, including replacement tokens, while preserving output diversity and adding no measurable inference latency.
problem_solved: LLM watermarking must remain detectable without biasing generated text or undermining fast inference. Speculative decoding adds a challenge: tokens replacing rejected drafts must retain the watermark without changing the draft acceptance rate.
method: Uses copula mixing and memoryless races as the core watermarking approach.
Keeps replacement tokens watermarked with the same keys during speculative decoding, while leaving the acceptance rate unchanged.
Builds on TextSeal’s diversity-preserving Gumbel-max scheme, addressing limitations of its coin-flip routing between two keys.
impact: TextSeal2 could help practitioners identify AI-generated text while retaining normal output diversity and speculative-decoding efficiency. The supplied abstract reports no measurable added inference latency, but is truncated before providing full methodological and evaluation details.

Three-icon strip highlighting preserved diversity, unchanged acceptance rate, and no measurable added latency.
paper_title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
paper_authors: Tom Sander, Pierre Fernandez, Itai Gat, Haiming Bao, Jiaxin Shi
